title: Adaptive hosted endpoints PRD: acceptance criteria, staged rollout & rollback playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: PRD for a single, unified Hosted Endpoints product that supports chat/completions/embeddings/rerank with adaptive runtime fallbacks, staged canary rollout, and an explicit rollback playbook. This ticket defines acceptance criteria, launch gating, scope decisions, and the step-by-step rollback procedure. It complements existing surface and contract specs and focuses on production readiness and customer-facing failure modes.
background: Multiple teams built endpoint surfaces independently. We need a unified hosted offering that guarantees consistent contracts while enabling the serving runtime to route to lower-cost or lower-latency model variants automatically. Prior PRDs covered API surface; this doc bridges product acceptance, operational gating, and post-launch rollback behavior focused on real customer SLAs and observed regressions.
goals: Ship hosted endpoints that: 1) expose a single API for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank; 2) maintain latency and quality SLOs; 3) support adaptive fallback to model variants under capacity or cost controls; 4) include deterministic acceptance tests and a clear rollback/mitigation path.
non_goals: This ticket does not: 1) redesign SDKs or add new client-side features beyond headers/flags for rollout; 2) change Dedicated/Private control planes; 3) implement new model training or evaluation tooling (only uses existing eval harness).
scope: In-scope: API contract validation, canary rollout plan, acceptance tests for latency/quality/cost, observability dashboards, alert thresholds, customer beta gating, rollback runbook. Out-of-scope: client SDK refactors, new UI Console flows (will be separate PM ticket).
scope_changes: 2025-02-25: Reduced initial canary cohort from 5% to 2% after ops sign-off to limit blast radius. 2025-02-28: Deferred SDK rollout header change to a follow-up to avoid coupling with this release. Changes documented here must be reflected in rollout plan and release notes.
acceptance_criteria: API contract matches spec: request/response shapes for chat, completion, embedding, rerank with documented examples and error codes.
Latency: p95 generation latency for chat/completions <= 350ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) on hosted tier under baseline load test.
Throughput: System sustains target QPS for tier (configurable) with autoscaling tested end-to-end using synthetic load.
Embeddings quality: on standard eval set, average cosine similarity between baseline and served embeddings >= 0.985; no regression >0.01 on any monitored customer probe set.
Rerank quality: NDCG@10 degradation <= 0.02 compared to baseline reranker on internal regression suite.
Fallbacks: Adaptive fallback to cheaper/quantized model variant must complete within 150ms of deciding to fallback and preserve request ordering guarantees for chat sessions.
Observability: Per-route dashboards activated (latency, error-rate, p99, cost-per-token) with synthetic canary probes and end-to-end trace links to request IDs.
Alerts & runbooks: PagerDuty escalation for error-rate >1% sustained for 5 minutes, latency p95 > 2x SLO for 10 minutes; runbook steps validated by SRE in a dry run.
Security: KMS key access and audit logging validated in staging; security review passed and documented in confluence link below.
Docs: Public API docs, quickstart, and example responses published and smoke-tested by Developer Experience team.
Customer beta: 3 pilot customers onboarded and exercised embedding/rerank flows for 2 weeks without major regressions.
Rollback validation: The rollback procedure must be tested in staging and meet the criteria in the rollback_playbook (each step completes in <10 minutes).
testing_plan: Unit + integration tests: validate contract and error pathways for all endpoint types.
Performance lab: iterative runs for baseline and worst-case scenarios including cold start, KV cache warmup, and batching variability.
Quality evals: run embedding cos-sim and rerank NDCG suites; store baselines and compare automatically as part of CI.
Canary probes: synthetic traffic that exercises chat statefulness, embeddings batch paths, and reranker score distribution.
Chaos exercise: simulate model variant OOM and forced fallback to assert system maintains request ordering and session continuity.
Security & compliance: key rotation test and audit-sink verification in pre-prod environment.
rollback_playbook: Step 0: Immediate triage — declare 'hosted-endpoints:major-regression' incident in Slack channel #incident-hosted-endpoints and assign SRE lead.
Step 1: Disable new rollout flag globally via feature toggle (console toggle or API) — this directs traffic back to previously stable model variant within 60s.
Step 2: If feature toggle fails, set routing policy to 'strict-stable' in routing control plane to avoid adaptive routing to experimental variants.
Step 3: If routing control plane unavailable, enact emergency traffic split: move traffic to Dedicated fallback pool or earlier snapshot image (documented AMI/container tag).
Step 4: Communicate: Send incident status to customers on pilot list, update public status page with mitigation steps and ETA.
Step 5: Post-mortem: capture root cause, regression metric deltas, and a remediation plan describing why acceptance tests missed this case.
launch_checklist: All acceptance criteria met and signed off by PM, Eng lead, SRE, and Security.
Canary rollout plan reviewed and approved with cohort sizes and automatic rollback triggers.
Monitoring dashboards created and documented with owner(s) and runbook links.
Billing: cost-per-token telemetry validated and limits configured for hosted tier.
Legal & compliance: SOC/enterprise checklist items verified for initial customers.
Customer communication: pilot invites drafted, onboarding runbooks prepared, support playbook created.
Release notes: internal and external notes drafted including known limitations and recommended params.
Post-launch observation window: 72 hours with elevated paging and daily check-ins scheduled.
open_questions: Q1: Do we require per-customer pinning to stable variants for all enterprise customers at GA or only for early pilots? (PM decision required)
Q2: What's the maximum acceptable cost uplift for enabling adaptive fallbacks by default? Need finance input to set default policy.
Q3: Should the embeddings regression threshold be relative to baseline or a hard cosine threshold for all models?
Q4: What is the expected experience for long-lived chat sessions if a fallback model has a different tokenizer/kv-cache characteristics? Need Eng design confirmation.
Q5: Which customers are in the initial pilot cohort? Sales to confirm with account teams.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Silent quality regressions from quantized variants. Mitigation: strict eval gating and per-customer pilot before global rollout.
Risk: Observability gaps hide regressions during burst traffic. Mitigation: synthetic traffic that mirrors peak usage and p99 tracing enabled.
Risk: Rollback toggles fail due to config propagation. Mitigation: pre-flight toggle exercise in staging and documented fallback routes.
Risk: Cost overruns when autoscaling to meet SLO. Mitigation: caps and alerts on cost-per-token and per-customer spend.
notes: This ticket intentionally prioritizes operational safety over fastest possible rollout. If acceptance tests reveal flaky regressions, we will extend pilot duration rather than widening the cohort. Any deviation from acceptance criteria requires explicit PM+Eng sign-off and an updated rollout amendment recorded here.
